blocks.text: The history of architectural technical lettering

Before CAD became the industry standard, architects drafted by hand. Every line and letter was a reflection of the architect's skill. Manual lettering styles were developed to be fast, clear, and uniform. Writing in all caps was the quickest way to maintain a consistent baseline and cap height across a drawing. It removed the variation found in lowercase letters where ascenders and descenders can clutter a page. This habit carried over into the digital era as a mark of professional identity.
Why standardization matters for construction documents

Drawings are legal documents. Ambiguous notes can lead to costly mistakes on site. If a contractor misreads a dimension or a material specification, the result is often expensive rework. Standardized lettering ensures that every person who touches the drawing, from the structural engineer to the subcontractor, interprets the data correctly. Consistency is not about aesthetics. It is about reducing risk and project liability.

items: Mixing fonts from different consultants or legacy files.

Using inconsistent line weights for text, making notes fade into the background.
Lack of a firm-wide CAD or BIM template for standard annotation styles.
Manual overrides in software that ignore global style settings.

blocks.text: How to fix lettering standards without buying new software

You can improve your documentation quality using tools you already have on your Mac. Start by defining a single font for all project documents. Use a sans-serif font like Arial or a dedicated architectural font that maintains clarity at small sizes. Set your text height to at least 1/8 inch for printed plans. This ensures that even after a print reduction from A1 to A3, the text remains readable.
Use the Annotative feature in AutoCAD or the Text Style settings in Archicad to lock text size to paper space. This prevents your notes from becoming illegible when you change your viewport scale.
blocks.title: Use annotative scaling

blocks.text: Create a master template file. Save your standard dimension styles, text styles, and layer settings within this file. Every time you start a new project, use this template as your base. This prevents the drift that happens when you copy drawings from old projects. If you find yourself manually changing text settings, stop and update your template instead.

faq.question: Why do architects use all caps instead of sentence case?
faq.answer: All caps provides a uniform visual block that is easier to read on busy construction site drawings. It also eliminates confusion between similar characters like 'l' and 'I'.

faq.question: Is it still necessary to use all caps in 2026?
faq.answer: While modern CAD software can handle any font, the industry standard remains all caps because it ensures consistent legibility across different printers and document scales.

faq.question: How can I fix inconsistent text across my project files?
faq.answer: Create a single master template with defined text styles. Use the 'Match Properties' tool in your software to quickly update existing text to match your new standard.
